Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Pentex Intrusion
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Master: trifle.
Put this card into play. When blood moves from a minion to a Methuselah's pool, half the blood (round down) goes to the blood bank. You may burn this card during your influence phase to gain 1 transfer.

(This isn't meant to be cumulative. Multiple copies of the card states the same thing: that you get only half the pool. Like stating multiple times (with multiple Torn Signpost) that a vampire's strength is set to 3.)

Flavor text: "Big Brother is Watching You." George Orwell, 1984

Art notes: A Ventrue in an office room, pulling from the wall a hidden wire that runs vertically to some hidden spying device. Some plaster is torn from the wall in the process. The Ventrue seems extremely upset.

World of Darkness reference: A Guide to Pentex

How does this card address a compelling game need?: Without affecting Blood Doll or Vessel, the card is meant to counter the Villen abuse that gives you 11-cap vampires for free. Pool management is now too easy and leads to massive pool gain that leads to time-limits. Inspired also by Extrala's post: vtesone.wordpress.com/2012/11/05/fattie-deck-building-template-modern-style/

Created by: Ankha

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
A way to make the card more interesting may be to rewrite it this way :

Name: Pentex Intrusion
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 1 pool
Master: trifle.
Put this card into play. When blood moves from a minion to a Methuselah's pool, for each blood the methuselah must remove the top card from its ash heap from play or burn 1 pool. You may burn this card during your influence phase to gain 1 transfer.

So, "regular" blood cycling should have all the card it need to power its blood recycling, and people who try to put 4 inner circle in play with the same 11 pool will have to actually play a lot of card to retrieve all that blood.

"top card" to avoid the card needing too much time for every villein.

It will impact a bit Ashur Tablet, but if you play Ashur tablet and are not greedy about pool cycling, it should be doable.

(of course, it's still a bit of a silver bullet. But it's a silver bullet that can be used to promote agressive play - after all, the best way to fill your ash heap is to play card - and the agression it generate can help the player manipulate the table the way he need it)

But then again, I do believe it's inaccurate to say that blood creation is the main problem that lead to people having 3+ 10cap or 11 cap on table. It's a combination of three things :

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
> I don't think it's that much true. Could you give any example?
> Personally, I play decks with 10/11 cap star vampire with no Villein with them that win tournaments or make the finals.
> Give me an example of a vampire that wouldn't be played if Villein was banned.

Surely crypts would evolve and less efficient vampires or those that enable cornercase master-requiring strategies would disappear, but nothing would be unplayable.

So I can't give an example because what would happen is that people would just flock back to Minion Tap, with the consequence that master variety goes down the drain again. Just as in the old day.

The last 3 years I've played more different masters than I ever did in the 15 years before that, simply because I can create my poolbuffer with trifle masters instead of being forced to use half of my MPA's on Minion Taps. The issue we are facing is that in a lot of circumstances the bonus master phase is used to simply undo the effects of the Villein instead of playing a different, exciting master.

The reality is, if you play anything bigger than, say, 6 caps, you NEED some way to get the pool back off of your vampires because otherwise you are just going to get ousted by dementation or Vignes. It's simply not optional and will never be as long as 2-caps can bleed for 5.

This can be done (and was done for years) by using Minion Tap, with extremely limited master selection as a result, leading to fairly boring deckbuilding in the green card section. Then Villein came along and dozens of master cards that were always nice and useful suddenly got a slot because people had master phases to spare! Rejoice!

Then some dumbfuck decided to make Lilith's Blessing tournament legal with the stupid state of VTES we have now as a result. Giant's Blood has always been a stupid card, but it was reasonable in the time where master slots were important for decks with fatties. Now it's just a lottery who gets to play with 10 extra pool. It's retarded, cannot be meta'd against and is *entirely* luck based. Once per game makes it even MORE retarded, not more balanced.

In case you haven't noticed, VEKN continues to create errata to the text of existing cards, errata that we all seem to accept.

I suggest that no card needs a new nerf card. If a card warps the play environment so much that people start dreaming up nerf cards, the best solution is to change the offending card itself. As I've already mentioned, we have quite a few new errata that aren't even nerfs - Psyche timing, ballots. Those are administrative changes.

Villein could be changed to move an exact amount of blood to a pool, probably 4. "Good" Villein users will be able to get back a casual pool buffer after playing a large-cap vampire (a vampire, who, apparently, could not possibly be worth the cost otherwise). Your 10-caps would cost 6, your 11-caps 7 - that's fair, isn't it? "Bad" Villein users will not be able to bring out as many IC members plus MMPA vamps in one game.

No extra nerf card for Villein is required to fill up valuable card slots in our libraries.

I would change it to "Move 4 (or 5, whatever) blood from this vampire to your pool", not "up to 4 blood". This is a trifle representing an elder vampire sucking down some younger blood quickly - you shouldn't get to choose how much you take.

If you must move 4 (or whatever), then there's no reason to stick with an "at least 2" concept. Obviously if you try to move 4 and the vampire has less than 4, you can only move as many counters as the vampire has. I think it's okay to suck the vampire dry or even fail to get any off the vampire at all. The modified effect isn't as good as normal Villein, so it shouldn't be hard to cycle.
